findings.text: Tasks with fresh log lines are marked stalled. In Servex/asks/tasks.js:383 (diff line 383), a task whose line 1 has no `agent` (or names an agent with no registry row) goes to `stalled()` with a null row, and stalled.js returns "no registry row" without checking the 2 h silence. The owner's rule needs all three: no line for 2 h AND not landed AND no live agent. The generated tasks.json shows the result: `2026-09-30/servex-mastermind` (last line 19:22, written one minute before generated_at) and `2026-10-02/panel2-sessions` (25 min old, the Dashboard task itself) are both top-scored "stalled". 16 of the 21 stalled rows say only `no registry row for owner "?"`. Fix: in task_state, when the row is null, call it stalled only if last_line_at is more than 2 h old (`stalled.SILENT_MS`). Then the "why" for a task with no owner can say "no owner agent, silent N min".

tasks.json is rewritten every minute inside public/, and that will probably reload the live site. LiveReload.js:144 only diverts `.jsonl` files to Tail. A `.json` change gets queued and broadcast as `changed`, and directory.json caused 203 reloads in one day for exactly this reason (LiveReload.js:192). `generated_at` changes on every tick, so the file is never the same twice. Fix: in write_tasks_json (tasks.js:418), skip the write when `tasks` is unchanged from what is already on disk, and/or confirm that no page reloads on that path.

The file is committed (diff: new file public/framework/ai/tasks.json, 1334 lines) even though it changes every tick. Every commit from the main tree will carry churn. Consider gitignoring it, the way a build artifact would be.

task_facts (tasks.js:332–361) re-implements the line walk in Asks.js `task_state()` (Asks.js:150), including the same chain of `at` fallbacks. Law 6 says one walker: export a shared one, or have Asks call tasks.js. The two already disagree on "landed": Asks also requires an `outcome`. The brief defines landed as a landed_at line, so tasks.js is correct here, but the duplicate will drift.

The test fixture (tasks.test.mjs) never covers the case in finding 1: a task with no agent and a fresh line. It also never covers an owner who is `dormant`. Add both, since they are the common real shapes.

The brief's items 3 and 5 hand-offs (a `send_to_agent` to @minion-card-pipeline and one message to @task-mastermind-panel2-sessions) can't be checked from the diff. Confirm they appear in task.jsonl, and send them only after finding 1 changes which rows are stalled.

The brief asks to parse `Budget:` from the first line. budget_of (tasks.js:319) matches it anywhere in the file, so a brief that quotes another task's "Budget: $N" in its body would be misread. Anchoring it to the first non-blank line is safer. Only 7 tasks have a budget today.
